extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, book reviewers, and members of the literary community interested in NBCC Awards eligibility and rules
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the National Book Critics Circle Awards' eligibility rules, eligible/excluded types of works, award categories, judge composition, and special awards (e.g., first-book prize). Useful for authors/publishers and critics preparing submissions or understanding qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for "the finest books and reviews published in English".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NBCC Awards are intended to promote what the organization considers the finest books and reviews published in English; the infobox statement frames the overall evaluative aim rather than a detailed scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and place eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Six awards are presented annually to books published in the U.S. during the preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible works must be books published in the United States in the calendar year prior to the award year (i.e., the awards recognize works published during the preceding calendar year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are for books and reviews published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While translations are considered (see inclusions), the overall award remit is to recognize works published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility — previously published in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Books previously published in English are not eligible, such as re-issues and paperback editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprints, re-issues, and paperback editions of works that have already appeared in English are excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre/form exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBCC does not consider "cookbooks, self help books (including inspirational literature), reference books, picture books or children's books".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly excluded from consideration even if otherwise published in the eligible time/place window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted special formats and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: They do consider "translations, short story and essay collections, self published books, and any titles that fall under the general categories".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite some exclusions, the NBCC explicitly accepts translations into English, collections (short stories, essays), and self-published books, as long as they fall within the general award categories and other eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Six main categories: Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Memoir/Autobiography, Biography, and Criticism; plus additional named prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NBCC presents awards in these principal categories each year; historically some category boundaries have shifted (e.g., Autobiography/Biography split into two awards after 2004). The organization also presents named prizes such as the John Leonard Prize (Best First Book), Ivan Sandrof Lifetime Achievement Award, Nona Balakian Citation for Excellence in Reviewing, and translation-related prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-book prize (John Leonard Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in 2014, the NBCC presents a special "first book" award across all six categories, named the John Leonard Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This special prize recognizes the best first book irrespective of the main category; eligibility is limited to authors' first books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible works include reviews (and citation for reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBCC's remit includes both books and reviews; there is also a Nona Balakian Citation for Excellence in Reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards program recognizes reviewing as part of its mission to promote criticism and literary culture; excellence in reviewing is separately honored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge composition and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges are the volunteer directors of the NBCC: 24 members serving rotating three-year terms, with eight elected annually by the voting members, namely 'professional book review editors and book reviewers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalists and winners are selected by this panel of NBCC directors who are professional reviewers/editors; their status as elected volunteers and term structure are part of the organization's governance that affects adjudication.
